sections.html:
Waukee is a Dallas County city on the west side of the Des Moines metro, and it has been one of the fastest-growing places in Iowa. The town was laid out in 1869 and incorporated in 1878, and it is believed to be named after the Milwaukee Road Railroad.

That makes Waukee the 16th-largest city in Iowa, covering about 22 square miles. With growth that quick, a large share of the houses are newer, and owners of older homes sit among many recent builds.

sections.h2: Home values and who buys here
sections.html:
Waukee has a median home value of $350,500 and a 66.5 percent owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $1,383 and median household income is $101,029. The median age was 33.9 in 2020, so the typical household is young.

About a third of occupied homes are rented, which means landlords and investors are active, and a fair share of Waukee sellers own a house they no longer live in. A job move is also a common reason people sell.

In 2017 Apple chose Waukee for a $1.38 billion data center campus, and the city's 2026 development list still shows an Apple site plan for a laydown area at West Hickman Road and Northwest 30th Street.

Retail is growing too. The same list includes a Walmart Supercenter site plan near Northeast Alice's Road and East Hickman Road, a Hy-Vee expansion within The Crossing at Alice's Road, and a Mid-American substation.

The city's 2026 project tracker shows plats, rezonings and site plans for both single-family and multi-family housing. Examples include The South 60 Plat 1 near Hickman Road, Trailridge Creek Plat 2, Alderbrook and Sugar Creek Landing.

  • Townhome projects include Maple Street Village and Triumph Village.
  • Multi-family projects include The Wren and Caliber Kettlestone.
  • Growth areas cluster around Kettlestone, Grand Prairie Parkway and Alice's Road.

If you want to sell an existing house here, new construction is part of the competition, since buyers can compare your house with homes still being platted.

The Waukee Community School District reports more than 13,600 students from preschool through grade 12 and over 2,200 staff, and calls itself the fastest-growing district in Iowa. It covers about 55 square miles and also serves students from Clive, Urbandale and West Des Moines, along with open-enrollment students.

It runs 10 elementary schools, four middle schools, Waukee High School and Waukee Northwest High School, which opened for the 2021 school year. Confirm your attendance area before listing, since boundaries cross city lines.

Waukee has no fixed-route city bus. HIRTA provides demand-response service, and the Des Moines Area Regional Transit Route 92 express serves Clive, about half a mile away. Most households rely on cars, so garage space and street access count here. Triangle Park in downtown Waukee and Waukee Stadium are local landmarks.

Waukee runs most permits through an online portal. Building permits cover single-family additions and alterations, accessory buildings, fences, decks, residential pools, hot tubs, signs and solar, among others. For roof replacement or basement finishing, contact the Building Official or the inspection hotline at 515-978-9533.

  • As of April 1, 2024, Community Development no longer issues irrigation meter permits for properties with a certificate of occupancy. Public Works handles those.
  • Underground irrigation systems need a reduced-pressure-zone backflow device.
  • Dog and cat licenses and urban chicken permits are issued through the city.

City Hall's main number is 515-978-7900 and Public Works is 515-978-7920. If previous owners built a deck or fence, check that a permit was pulled before a buyer asks.

sections.h2: Documents to gather before you sell
sections.html:
• Your latest Dallas County tax statement and proof of the first-half and second-half payments.
  • Any permit records for decks, fences, additions or pools.
  • Mortgage payoff statement and the names on the title.
  • Plat and covenant details if your lot is in an association.

Your closing agent orders the title work. Having these items ready helps with any sale route.

Property tax in Dallas County comes due in two parts, September 1 and March 1, going delinquent after September 30 and March 31. The monthly interest rate is 1.5 percent, and only the postmark date counts for mailed payments. The Treasurer's office is at 800 Court Street, Suite 111, in Adel, phone 515-993-5808.

The state transfer tax is 80 cents per $500 of value beyond the first $500. The seller, buyer or agent signs a declaration of value, which is filed with the deed at the recorder.

A seller's written disclosure under Iowa Code 558A.4 reaches items such as significant structural defects and lead service lines. Your closing agent can tell you whether it applies.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Waukee
sections.html:
Start with the address and a short description of the house: age, condition, whether it is occupied, and any loan against it. We review the property and the title and send a written offer. You can say no at no cost.

If you accept, a title company orders the title work, confirms who is on the deed and asks the lender for a payoff figure. You pick a closing date that suits your move. At closing you sign the deed, the title company pays off the mortgage and any tax balance, and the remaining money goes to you.

No buyer's lender is involved, so there is no appraisal to wait for and no loan to fall through. That helps in a market where new builds compete with resale homes and buyers have plenty of choices.

Many Waukee houses sit in platted subdivisions, and some lots carry covenants or association rules. Gather the plat and covenant details early, since a title company will ask for them. If a deck, fence or pool was added after purchase, confirm the permit history with the city so the paperwork matches what stands on the lot.

For a house in an area still being platted, such as the Kettlestone or Grand Prairie Parkway corridors, expect buyers to compare your finishes and lot against brand-new homes nearby. Sellers who would rather not compete on price and staging often find the as-is route simpler.

Listing the traditional way can work for a well-kept house in a fast-growing market, though commission and a buyer's loan timeline come with it. Selling on your own skips the commission. A cash sale suits owners who inherited, own a rental, or do not want to spend on repairs, and it removes the lender step.

Ask each option for a written net figure and closing date.

faqs.q: Which county handles property tax for Waukee?
faqs.a: Dallas County. The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with interest of 1.5 percent per month after each deadline.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a deck or fence in Waukee?
faqs.a: Yes. Both are on the city's building permit list and are submitted through the online portal.
The 2020 census counted 23,940 people, and the 2024 estimate is 34,420, which makes Waukee the 16th-largest city in Iowa.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Waukee?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes had a $350,500 median value for 2020 to 2024. Yours may be worth more or less.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Waukee houses?
faqs.a: The Waukee Community School District spans about 55 square miles, taking in parts of Clive, Urbandale and West Des Moines, so confirm your address with the district.
